title: Immutep Receives A$2.16 million French R&D Tax Incentive
body_markdown:
**SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA, Oct. 28, 2026 —**[Immutep Limited](https://www.immutep.com/) (ASX: IMM; NASDAQ: IMMP) (“Immutep” or “the Company”), a clinical-stage immunotherapy company targeting cancer and autoimmune diseases, today announced that it has received a cash payment of €1.36 million (approximately A$2.16 million) from the French Government under its Crédit d’Impôt Recherche (CIR) research tax incentive program, for eligible R&D activities conducted in calendar year 2025.


The CIR is a French Government incentive that refunds companies 30% of their eligible R&D expenditure. Immutep is eligible through its French subsidiary, Immutep S.A.S., which conducts research at its laboratory in France.


The CIR payment follows Immutep’s receipt of A$0.86 million cash rebate under the Australian Government’s R&D Tax Incentive, announced on 30 September 2026. Immutep’s German subsidiary, Immutep GmbH, is also eligible for Germany’s R&D tax incentive (Forschungszulage).


The non-dilutive funding will be applied to Immutep’s current R&D activities for its product candidates, eftilagimod alfa (efti) and IMP761.


Immutep’s expected cash reach extends into the first half of CY2028.


**About Immutep**
Immutep is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. The Company is a pioneer in the understanding and advancement of therapeutics related to Lymphocyte Activation Gene-3 (LAG-3), and its diversified product portfolio harnesses LAG-3’s ability to stimulate or suppress the immune response. Immutep is dedicated to leveraging its expertise to bring innovative treatment options to patients in need and to maximise value for shareholders. For more information, please visit[www.immutep.com](https://www.immutep.com/) .
